UCLA Rig: Probe Sync Offset, Aug–Oct 2023

electrophysiology
synchronization
QC
Neuropixels
spikeglx
Every Neuropixels recording made on the churchlandlab_ucla rig with SpikeGLX 20201103 after the base-station firmware 3.2.186 update has spikes shifted by whole 0.5 s sync periods: 29 sessions, 50 insertions, MFD_05–09 (BWM) and MM012 (U19 chronic).
Author

Olivier Winter

Published

November 6, 2026

Between 2023-08-15 and 2023-10-20, every probe recorded on the churchlandlab_ucla rig with SpikeGLX 20201103 and base-station firmware 3.2.186 has its spikes shifted on the session clock by whole 0.5 s sync half-periods. That is 29 sessions and 51 probes, with no exceptions. Trials, wheel and video are correct; spike times are not. The “viz” links open the trial viewer and are only given for insertions in the BWM 2023 release (13 pids).

What it looks like

The same signature shows up across the BWM release. The feedback (valve click) evokes a sharp population transient that should sit at 0 s. A handful of insertions have it at about +0.5 s:

Cause

All UCLA 2023 recordings used one PXIe base station (SN 21230842):

period SpikeGLX BSC firmware probes shifted
2023-06-01 → 2023-08-13 20201103 3.2.176 46 0
2023-08-14 → 2024-05-16 20230411 3.2.186 790 0
2023-08-15 → 2023-10-20 20201103 3.2.186 51 51

Installing SpikeGLX 20230411 flashed the base-station firmware to 3.2.186. The MFD and MM012 experiments kept running the old 20201103 install on that updated base station. With that combination, SpikeGLX opens the probe file one or more sync fronts away from the nidq file. ibllib version3B pairs fronts by index from the start of the file, so the sync passes QC with flat residuals while every spike is offset by k × 0.5 s. The main analysis has the mechanism, the wheel validation and the census of all 3B probes.

Fix

Re-run version3B on the existing _spikeglx_sync.* datasets, pairing fronts with the lag in the table (+0.5 s ⇒ drop the first probe front). Then re-interpolate spikes.times. No re-sorting and no raw data are needed.

Other BWM-release insertions

Besides the 13 above, 4 BWM-release insertions are shifted by the sporadic mechanism B, which is not rig-specific. That makes 17 in total.

Between 2023-08-15 and 2023-10-20, every probe recorded on the `churchlandlab_ucla` rig with **SpikeGLX `20201103`** and
**base-station firmware `3.2.186`** has its spikes shifted on the session clock by whole 0.5 s sync half-periods.
That is 29 sessions and 51 probes, with no exceptions. Trials, wheel and video are correct; spike times are not.
The "viz" links open the trial viewer and are only given for insertions in the BWM 2023 release (13 pids).

## Affected insertions

::: {.column-page}
{{< include ucla_rig_pids.md >}}
:::

One recording, MFD_07 2023-08-30 ([c8372676-0e5b-47dd-824b-08f841e5b572](https://alyx.internationalbrainlab.org/admin/actions/session/c8372676-0e5b-47dd-824b-08f841e5b572/change/)),
is also shifted but has no registered insertion. Download: [probe table](ucla_rig_probes.csv) · [session table](ucla_rig_sessions.csv).

## What it looks like

![[92822789-608f-44a6-ad64-fe549402b2df MFD_05/2023-08-16/001 probe00](https://viz.internationalbrainlab.org/app?spikesorting=ss_2024-05-06&dset=bwm&pid=92822789-608f-44a6-ad64-fe549402b2df&tid=0&cid=0&qc=0#trialviewer), from the IBL viz site. Population responses start ~0.55 s after stimulus onset and ~0.5 s after first movement, and the sharp feedback transient sits at +0.5 s instead of 0. The whole raster is late by one sync half-period.](figures/viz_92822789-608f-44a6-ad64-fe549402b2df_trial_event_plot.png)

The same signature shows up across the BWM release. The feedback (valve click) evokes a sharp population transient
that should sit at 0 s. A handful of insertions have it at about +0.5 s:

![Feedback-aligned population rate for BWM insertions, from the repeated-site decoding-power project. Left: time of the sharpest feedback transient (> 6 SD) per insertion. Right: feedback-aligned PSTHs, with the flagged insertions in red.](figures/feedback_transient_qc.png)

## Cause

All UCLA 2023 recordings used one PXIe base station (SN 21230842):

| period | SpikeGLX | BSC firmware | probes | shifted |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 2023-06-01 → 2023-08-13 | `20201103` | `3.2.176` | 46 | 0 |
| 2023-08-14 → 2024-05-16 | `20230411` | `3.2.186` | 790 | 0 |
| **2023-08-15 → 2023-10-20** | **`20201103`** | **`3.2.186`** | **51** | **51** |

Installing SpikeGLX `20230411` flashed the base-station firmware to `3.2.186`. The MFD and MM012 experiments kept
running the old `20201103` install on that updated base station. With that combination, SpikeGLX opens the probe
file one or more sync fronts away from the nidq file. ibllib `version3B` pairs fronts by index from the start of
the file, so the sync passes QC with flat residuals while every spike is offset by k × 0.5 s. The
[main analysis](index.qmd) has the mechanism, the wheel validation and the census of all 3B probes.

## Fix

Re-run `version3B` on the existing `_spikeglx_sync.*` datasets, pairing fronts with the lag in the table
(+0.5 s ⇒ drop the first probe front). Then re-interpolate `spikes.times`. No re-sorting and no raw data are needed.
